Hi Maria,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Follow-up from Redwood on next steps for the Azure private plan order and how billing should flow. To keep procurement moving, we want to propose an execution approach that balances AstraHealth's AP preferences and the Marketplace/co-sell implications:

- Preferred billing cadence: monthly invoices, Net 30 (Astra standard). If Astra requires milestone invoicing we can support a staggered schedule (40% upfront, 30% on production acceptance, 30% 30 days after go-live) — we'll need that captured in the order form.
- Marketplace billing model: two options (merchant-of-record via Azure Marketplace OR publisher invoices directly). Merchant-of-record is typically smoother for customers but has implications for how co-sell attribution and payouts are recorded.
- PO & remit: please confirm the exact PO name and remit address we should reference on invoices. If Astra needs invoices routed through a specific vendor code or AP inbox, share that so we can map in our billing system.
- Contract execution: we can push the Order Form + Commercial Exhibit to DocuSign for Maria (Legal) and the Astra PO for AP. If there are legal redlines beyond a handful of standard items we prefer those handled as a short addendum to avoid delaying onboarding.

Attached: Private-Plan-Order-Form-v3.pdf (draft), Redwood-Marketplace-FAQ.pdf (billing model summary).

Would you prefer merchant-of-record via Azure for year 1 to simplify AP, or publisher-billed invoices directly to Astra? If merchant is fine, we will proceed with monthly invoices Net30 and route via Azure's marketplace flow.

I can hop on a quick call with Azure billing if helpful — looping Matt Lewis from Microsoft here.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi all,

Short note from the Marketplace ops side to clarify billing models:

1) Merchant-of-Record (Azure charges the customer): Azure acts as the payment processor and issues a single invoice to the customer. This is usually fastest for customer procurement teams — invoice matching is straightforward for customers, and Marketplace handles tax collection in many jurisdictions. For partners, revenue reconciliation goes through the Marketplace settlement.

2) Publisher billing (partner invoices customer directly): Redwood would invoice Astra directly. This gives Redwood more control over billing and is sometimes preferred for specific contractual terms, but customers must accept an external invoice workflow and it can delay PO issuance. Co-sell attribution can still be recorded, but payout mechanics differ.

For Astra's scenario (enterprise procurement + intention to run with committed capacity), merchant-of-record is a low-friction choice. A few asks: please confirm whether Astra needs invoices to reference a specific vendor ID and whether they require a separate tax ID on each invoice. Also see attached ops note for edge cases (marketplace-billing-ops.pdf).

Happy to join a short call to walk procurement through the merchant flow.

- Matt
Marketplace Program Manager — Microsoft

2) Commercial commitments: Redwood will accept monthly billing Net30 for subscription charges. For the onboarding SOW (professional services), we can use milestone invoices if Astra prefers.

3) Co-sell / compensation: Redwood requests that co-sell attribution for the HUB deal (HB-15432-AH) be recorded so partner payouts and internal credits are preserved. Laura, can you prepare a short co-sell exhibit to attach to the order form?

Maria — once procurement confirms the PO name and remit email, we will push the Order Form to DocuSign to you and your signatory. Ben, can you please join to handle any billing field updates required by Astra's questionnaire?
